pre_confirmation_amendment.reason: the spent posthoc analyzer knew ABCD and evaluated only the known-wrong orientation; a deployable chronology method cannot use the unknown true order to choose which orientation to test
pre_confirmation_amendment.correction: for every unordered stage pair, solve both orientation classes; infer an orientation only when exactly one class is certified impossible; abstain when neither is excluded; mark invalid when both are excluded

method_components.witness_bank: unit witness directions derived from K3 class geometry and frozen before any K4 output
method_components.higher_order_acquisition: witness-projected degree-4 interactions from exact measured prefixes
method_components.relaxation: K-local order marginal polytope with simplex and marginal-consistency equalities
method_components.certificate: proof-safe infinity-norm multi-witness LP with independently corrected dual lower bound
method_components.pairwise_decision: for each unordered pair {i,j}, independently certificate-test both i<j and j<i classes without access to the true chronology label
method_components.chronology_rule: infer the surviving orientation only if exactly one pair class is certified impossible; return a total chronology only when every unordered pair is certified and the inferred orientations form one transitive total order; otherwise abstain; both orientations excluded is invalid

source_spent_result.posthoc_pairwise_note: the spent analysis used the known target only for method development/evaluation; confirmation must use the label-blind two-sided pair interface

numerical_rules.pair_status_certified: exactly one of the two orientation classes has corrected lower bound greater than elimination_guard
numerical_rules.pair_status_ambiguous: neither orientation class is certified impossible
numerical_rules.pair_status_invalid: both orientation classes are certified impossible

complexity_claim.explicit_limitation: for N>K, exact true-history certification additionally requires control of omitted interactions above degree K; no universal finite bound is claimed

method_change_policy_after_confirmation_: no changes to mathematics, witness construction, thresholds, pairwise two-sided decision rule, target set, or interpretation based on heldout outputs; any later method revision requires a new explicitly labeled development phase and new untouched confirmation data
